choice_basis: Bear: one row per hunt [null, license applicants, licenses awarded]; MDNR publishes only totals plus the point range of resident and nonresident winners ('Points for Award', in pts_res / pts_nr) and the resident/nonresident award counts (drawn_res / drawn_nr). Elk: rows are [points, eligible applicants, drawn] where points = prior unsuccessful years (chances in the weighted drawing = points + 1).

sources.label: MDNR: Application period for Michigan elk hunt opens Friday (Apr 28, 2026)

notes: Bear (system preference): applicants with most points drawn first; nonresidents may receive up to 5% of licenses in each hunt. 72,580 total bear applicants in 2026, 45,271 of them point-only; 0 leftover licenses.
Bear applicant counts per hunt are not split by residency, so rows are in 'all'; res/nr award counts and point ranges are extra fields.

Elk (system weighted random, residents only): one statewide pool per license type; applicants get 1 chance + 1 per prior unsuccessful year since 2003 (max 24 chances in 2026). Antlerless pool = applicants who chose 'bull or antlerless' and were not drawn for any-elk. Hunt-period breakdown of applicants is not published.
Elk any-elk table total chances printed as 412,775 while the summary says 412,755 (agency inconsistency).
